name: Swarnapureeswarar Temple, Andankoil (Tirukkaduvaaikkaraiputtur)
deity: Shiva as Swarnapureeswarar (lord of the golden city), with the goddess Swarnambikai (Sivasekari)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Andankoil, the Tevaram's Tirukkaduvaaikkaraiputtur, near Valangaiman, honours Shiva as Swarnapureeswarar — the lord of the golden city — with the goddess Swarnambikai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Appar, its legend joins it to the great Thyagaraja temple of Tiruvarur, built here, by tradition, by the minister Kandadeva at the lord's command in a dream.

sections.history: Andankoil, whose Tevaram name is Tirukkaduvaaikkaraiputtur (Thiru Kaduvai Karai Thenputhur), lies in the Valangaiman taluk of Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar). By tradition the temple is linked to the building of the great Thyagaraja temple at Tiruvarur, and the stone shrine is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Swarnapureeswarar — 'lord of the golden city' — in the sanctum, with the goddess Swarnambikai, also called Sivambigai, Sivasekari and Poornambikai, in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The golden names of lord and goddess give the shrine its character.
sections.legends: The sthala legend joins Andankoil to Tiruvarur. When the minister Kandadeva was building the great Thyagaraja temple at Tiruvarur, he came to this place to gather stone and lime for the work; and here Shiva appeared to him in a dream and bade him raise a temple, which he did — the shrine of Swarnapureeswarar. The lord's name Swarnapureeswarar and the goddess Swarnambikai, both 'golden,' keep the memory of that sacred commission.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine near Valangaiman. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail include Andankoil among their stops.
sections.experience: At Andankoil the pilgrim finds a golden-named shrine bound to the story of great Tiruvarur. Before Swarnapureeswarar and Swarnambikai, the visitor remembers the minister who gathered stone here and raised a temple at the lord's own command — a quiet delta sanctuary with a golden heart.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Andankoil is in the Valangaiman taluk of Tiruvarur district (Thirukaduvaikaraithenputhur, PIN 612804), near Valangaiman. Valangaiman and Kumbakonam are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
